item.title: Fortnite Brainrot Card Tycoon Codes
item.description:
Fortnite Brainrot Card Tycoon is a Creative Map made by PWR that puts a fresh spin on the classic Brainrot formula. In this game, you can collect cards, farm cash, and upgrade your cards for even bigger bonuses. That's not all, however, as there are also a bunch of codes hidden around the map, granting you instant rewards. Here's every code in Fortnite Brainrot Card Tycoon.

Fortnite 1V1 With Every Gun (All Codes & Secrets)

There is a roster of secret items that players can get in Fortnite's 1V1 With Every Gun by Hive. Here is how to get each one.

8
By Nathan Round

All Brainrot Card Tycoon Codes in Fortnite

Brainrot Card Tycoon has a bunch of codes that players can use to earn free Gems, Gold, Card Packs, and much more. Each code can be found throughout the game's world , with the potential for some to remain completely secret in future updates. However, to save you time, we've provided a list of every working code below.

As a reminder, all codes in Brainrot Card Tycoon could potentially expire at a later date. New codes will likely be added in the future, so be sure to check back regularly to stay up to date.

All Working Codes

383963

20 Gems

136044

30 Gems

449394

20,000 Gold

235909

Rainbow Apprentice Pack

760608

Rainbow Tim Cheese Pack

942048

2x Golden Artisan Packs

All Expired Codes

There are currently no expired codes for Brainrot Card Tycoon. Make sure to return to this guide regularly to find out which codes are no longer working.

How to Use Codes in Fortnite Brainrot Card Tycoon

To redeem codes in Brainrot Card Tycoon, head to the Codes Terminal. You can find it in the game's main lobby. Once you're at the terminal, simply manually enter the code you want to redeem and submit it.

Once you have redeemed a code, any Gems or Gold rewards will be added to your inventory right away. However, if you receive a Card Pack, you will need to equip them and then press the Use Button to place them down on your base. From here, wait till each card is ready to be claimed, or speed up the process by pickaxing each one , and then open the card to recieve it.

Remember, as with any Fortnite Creative game, all codes in Brainrot Card Tycoon are one-time use, and you cannot bypass this restriction by switching servers. If you haven't played Brainrot Card Tycoon yet, use the Map Code below to jump in.

item.title: 6 Best Open-World RPGs With Superb Stories, Ranked
item.description:
Open-world RPGs usually occupy a conflicted spot, having to balance the freedom to go almost anywhere with gripping character-driven narratives that keep players hooked and dedicated to their overarching goal. While it’s not unusual for such games to lean more heavily toward one aspect, like Elden Ring trading classic storytelling for something more subtle, there are also great open-world role-playing games that walk the perfect line between these core pillars.

That said, certain studios have become all but synonymous with superb stories placed into vast worlds driven by freedom and curiosity, CD Projekt Red in particular. By mastering the narrative flow so it doesn’t get lost or sidelined during free-form exploration, the open-world RPGs below are already some of the best available to play today. Their stories are definitely among the biggest attractions: focused, intriguing, and featuring some of the most compelling characters in the genre.

6 Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth

Even Those Who Never Played It Know Cloud, Tifa, and Aerith

The latest Final Fantasy installments, FF15 and FF16, have received a pretty mixed reception among long-term fans, yet the iconic series still stands as a pinnacle of the genre thanks to the ongoing FF14 and the FF7 remake trilogy. With Revelation already looming on the horizon and promising to wrap up one of the best stories and character journeys in a satisfying way, Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth is easily among the best open-world RPGs of this generation.

Nostalgia aside, it is a true celebration of cinematic, refined narrative, expanded character arcs that hit differently but equally strong, and a wealth of open-world content. It’s like stepping straight into an animated movie and living another life in a distant world. While the original FF7 is widely considered among the best JRPGs ever made, largely for its standout story and characters, there are a few caveats to consider when approaching Rebirth .

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's "Bigger" Open World Doesn't Have to Be a Bad Thing

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's larger world may sound daunting, but Rebirth already proved that bigger doesn't have to mean worse.

By Josh Cotts

Naturally, it is just the second part of the remake trilogy, so playing FF7 Remake beforehand will make for a much better experience overall and a more cohesive overarching story. Even if it is massively expanded in every aspect, Rebirth would hardly work entirely as a standalone game for complete newcomers. Players would miss out on the key character introductions, the establishment of their relationships, and the vital prologue to the whole Sephiroth arc.

5 Fallout: New Vegas

Finally Reaching New Vegas Feels Like a Game Within a Game

Like most Bethesda games, both Fallout 3 and Fallout 4 are great open-world RPGs, but hardly special for their stories alone. Obsidian’s Fallout: New Vegas , though, is quite a different beast.

With exploration and freedom that rival the other Fallout games, New Vegas absolutely delivers with its main storyline too, fueled by mystery, intrigue, and a brutal introduction. As the Courier, who is shot in the head and left for dead right at the start, you are drawn into an ongoing investigation of what went wrong, only to find yourself amid a much larger faction confrontation for control over the Mojave portion of the post-nuclear wasteland.

Obsidian's New Fallout Game Is Actually a Bigger Deal Than Fallout 5

Obsidian is finally making another Fallout game, and a new Todd Howard interview makes it sound even more important that Fallout 5.

By LB Beistad

After the impactful intro, Fallout: New Vegas starts pretty slowly but quickly gains momentum. By the time you reach New Vegas itself, it feels like you’ve already experienced an entire game’s worth of story and quests. Yet things only get more tricky, tangled, and intense in the heart of Nevada. Coupled with the game’s standout role-playing possibilities, this freedom is reflected throughout the story as well, with numerous possible branches, alliances, and even betrayals. With Fallout: New Vegas Remastered now officially confirmed, it’s just a matter of time until fans can return to this unique and beloved RPG.

4 NieR: Automata

Piecing a Giant Puzzle Together From Different Perspectives

NieR: Automata is a bit of a different kind of open-world RPG, both in its map structure and its narrative flow. Known for its unique storytelling that requires several playthroughs for characters such as 2B, 9S, and A2 to fully piece the entire story together, this layer is the glue of the entire experience.

Once the game gets its hooks into you, it’ll be hard not to see it through. Especially given how every new run sheds more light on unanswered questions, adding fresh perspectives and facets to the already familiar characters, events, and even enemies and bosses, sometimes turning them completely upside down.

NieR: Automata - All Playable Characters

There are three playable characters in NieR: Automata; here's who they are and how to switch between them.

By Joshua Leeds

While there is definitely some exploration freedom involved, NieR: Automata is almost entirely driven by its complex storytelling, exploring mature and philosophical themes with a lingering depth that stays with you. It’s also a fascinating case of a game that works beautifully on its own, but previous installments vastly enrich the impression through subtle details and smart nods.

​​​​​​​In case you missed it, some form of continuation to NieR: Automata has been officially teased by Square Enix recently, and I personally can’t wait to see Yoko Taro’s next spin on this fascinating universe.

3 Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty

Expansion So Good It Feels Not Enough to Leave Us With Just One

Cyberpunk 2077 is actually a bright example of two largely conflicting pillars, with its open-world design often at odds with the main story centered around the pressing urge to find a solution for V’s unique condition. The sprawling main narrative, with its branching paths for V to take, is still among the best in the genre from the past few years.

True to CD Projekt Red’s hallmarks, the game’s expansion Phantom Liberty doubles down on everything great about the original. It often feels like a full-fledged sequel and a significant step forward for this world’s potential. Set amid Night City’s densest and most packed district, Dogtown, Phantom Liberty’s storyline is largely standalone, although it has strong personal hooks for V to get involved, as well as a bonus ending for the main game.

Cyberpunk 2077's Cancelled DLC 2 is the Silver Lining that Sets the Stage for Cyberpunk 2

Cyberpunk 2077's canceled second DLC serves as a great staging ground for a location or story in the eventual release of Cyberpunk 2.

By Nick Rodriguez

For the events of the expansion, V works alongside new characters: sleeper agent Solomon Reed, brilliant netrunner Song So Mi, and even NUSA president Rosalind Myers. Choosing who to side with is a big deal in Phantom Liberty , as it unlocks different story branches, and it’s hard to say which path is the best. One thing is for certain, though: you’ll hardly forget the chain of events across the next 25 hours of this standout RPG story.

2 Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2

Proving It’s Possible to Have a Reactive World and Gripping Story All at Once

The Kingdom Come: Deliverance series is mostly well-known for its authentic medieval setting with no magic or fantasy elements in sight, as well as for its immersiveness, which is at times quite brutal. Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 , though, has taken quite a few steps toward the best open-world RPG narratives out there, packing in a surprisingly cinematic, epic, and unpredictable character-driven storyline. While it’s just as fun to simply live your daily life as Henry of Skalitz in KCD 2 as it was in the original, the game offers so much more.

Kingdom Come: Salvation's Leaked Title Basically Confirms Its Story

The next Kingdom Come game's apparent title leak points toward a story Warhorse may have been quietly building toward since the original game began.

By Josh Cotts

Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is a textbook example of having the best of both worlds: an immersive and reactive world for free-form exploration and character growth, paired with an intense, lengthy main story full of gripping pacing, emotional depth, and strong character dynamics. With no permanent companions, the game focuses on a handful of deeply developed recurring characters. Almost like The Witcher 3 , KCD 2 is built to intertwine its many questlines, making them constantly cross paths in the most unpredictable ways.

To top things off, like the best RPGs out there, Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is unafraid to completely emotionally wreck you, adding moral complexity that makes every choice feel truly impactful.

1 The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Hearts of Stone

Might Be the Best RPG Storyline of Them All

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is among the most celebrated open-world RPGs ever made, praised for its branching and overarching narrative. CDPR’s achievements are truly generational here, with both main and side quests equally satisfying and interesting, driven by strong writing, memorable characters, and unique twists.

While the game’s main story is undoubtedly great and already deserves a top spot on this list, its expansions are even better. Blood and Wine is usually the fan favorite for its scope, but Hearts of Stone is probably one of my favorite narrative pieces ever done by CDPR so far. Completely standalone, this focused expansion introduces new faces and conflicts, with Geralt getting involved in an overarching investigation to lift a curse.

The Witcher Remake Needs Resident Evil's Restraint, Not Wild Hunt's Scale

The Witcher Remake going full open world risks losing the very things that made the original special.

By Vlad Mazanko

You’ll find yourself amid a sprawling narrative full of intrigue, while the stage is set for standout characters like Olgierd von Everec and Gaunter O’Dimm to truly shine. Each new quest is as unpredictable as it is fun, featuring intricate robberies, spirit possessions, lighthearted and deeply tragic human moments, all sprinkled with some of the best boss fights in the game.

It’s slightly unfair to compare this dedicated 15-hour questline to 100-hour full games, yet to this day, Hearts of Stone’s story remains among my personal favorites in the entire genre. Will the upcoming Songs of the Past manage to top it?

item.title: Psychonauts Developer Double Fine Hit With Layoffs
item.description:
Double Fine, the developer responsible for games like the Psychonauts franchise , Brutal Legend , and most recently Kiln , is cutting about a third of its overall staff in layoffs. The move comes following the reveal that the Psychonauts developer would be parting ways with Xbox.

Double Fine was originally bought by Xbox back in 2019. The studio successfully released three titles during its time with Xbox, including the long-awaited Psychonauts 2 , plus Keeper and Kiln . Back in June 2026, Double Fine responded to rumors of being potentially shut down with just an emoji, but it was later revealed that the studio was going independent again, instead.

Xbox CEO Reveals Full Details of Layoffs and Restructuring

In a letter to employees, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirms the single biggest staff reduction event for the company as well as four studios leaving.

By Derek Nichols

Double Fine Productions Reveals Layoffs

Double Fine Productions has announced that the team let go of 23 staff members in necessary layoffs. In a message shared on official social media channels, Double Fine founder Tim Schafer explained that the team is tightly-knit, and that the decision to let members go was not made lightly. However, it became necessary in order for Double Fine as a whole to survive. Now that Double Fine no longer has support from Xbox, it seems the studio couldn't maintain the same size of team it had, which was somewhere around 90 people. Schafer noted that the studio would be supporting those impacted as much as possible, and that they would be missed at the game studio.

GameRant Quiz

This development is just the latest in the fallout following Xbox's restructuring. Compulsion Games exited and became independent again like Double Fine, while Undead Labs and Ninja Theory have "entered terms to join new ownership." Xbox as a whole is experiencing somewhere around 3,200 layoffs, and concerns have arisen regarding the studios remaining with Xbox and how all these cuts will impact their business. Zenimax Media developers have claimed that the studio lost tremendous knowledge and expertise from the cuts, and Bethesda and Obsidian have allegedly been left trying to pick up the pieces after the fact.

While Double Fine's losses are due to the departure from Xbox, game development as a whole has been suffering considerably in recent years. Numerous studios, publishers, and company owners have enacted significant cuts to teams, sometimes following the release of successful games. In other cases, game development studios have been completely shut down. Current difficulties with insufficient supply of parts and high expenses for components like RAM have also had an impact, delaying systems like the Steam Machine and potentially causing headaches for future consoles, like the next PlayStation and Xbox systems.

For now, it remains to be seen what the future will look like for Double Fine. The studio's most recent game, Kiln , saw largely positive reviews from critics, and currently holds a Mostly Positive score on Steam. However, the game also struggled to find an audience, reaching a player count of just 193 unique users on launch day. That number has since plummeted further, with the game holding a 24-hour peak of just 13 players on Steam as of publication time. Even with the team losses and recent release struggles, though, Double Fine has previously found success with crowdfunding, so its fans may come through for it if necessary.

item.title: Pokemon TCG Shop Offers Cash Bounty for Thief's Capture
item.description:
A Pokemon trading card shop in Japan is offering a cash reward for anyone who successfully captures a thief that broke into the store. While burgled card shops typically work with the police to try and find the culprit, this is an unusual move for a Pokemon TCG store to make.

Card thieves breaking into stores to steal high-value Pokemon cards has become unfortunately common news in recent years. Generally, these thefts are committed while stores are closed, or the thieves choose to break into Pokemon TCG store warehouses rather than storefronts. While it's always a relief when no one is harmed during moments like these, some business owners seem to be getting more than fed up with the prevalence of theft.

Pokemon TCG Thieves Arrested After Stealing Over $200k in Cards

A pair of thieves have been arrested in Japan following a heist involving a collection of Pokemon cards valued at more than $200k.

By Marc Deschamps

Pokemon TCG Shop Offers Cash Reward for Thief's Capture

Now, a store in Japan called Kaitorip is offering a 1 million yen bounty for a thief that broke in on July 22. Kaitorip has shared surveillance footage of the thief making off with cards, as well as the broken front door that they got in through. The store owner has stipulated that the thief must be handed over alive in order to receive the 1 million yen bounty, which converts to about $6,100 USD. The shop is also offering a secondary reward of 50,000 yen for anyone who has solid information on the thief's identity, or roughly $305 USD.

Though this and every other Pokemon TCG theft are unfortunate situations, it could have been worse. The details indicate that this theft transpired at about 3 in the morning. Unfortunately, in some cases, brazen robbers have actually stolen Pokemon cards from stores while they've been open, terrorizing and sometimes even injuring employees and customers in the process. Thankfully, it seems that no one was harmed or put in physical danger in this case in Japan.

While Pokemon card thefts are a serious problem that needs to be resolved somehow, it's not the only difficulty facing the card game. The scalping of Pokemon TCG has been bad enough to gain the attention of the government of Japan, which is putting together a task force to combat scalping. Individual stores and The Pokemon Company itself are also cracking down, with implemented measures ranging from requiring customers to correctly answer Pokemon quizzes or as extreme as requiring government IDs or instituting facial recognition scans of Pokemon TCG buyers. Time will tell if these efforts — and the card shop bounty being offered — create the results the card game needs.

item.title: Brand-New Free Zombie Co-Op Game Launches to Mostly Positive Reviews on Steam
item.description:
The best zombie games know that, sometimes, it's just fun to squad up with some buddies and gun down some zombies, and it's that core premise of the genre that a new zombie co-op game leans into heavily. Available completely free of charge on Steam , it's noteworthy that this free game has launched to Mostly Positive reviews via Steam's review rating system (with a good volume of user reviews to boot, too).

Of course, as a free-to-play game on Steam, it's worth mentioning that this new title has to make money somehow, but at least as of this writing, its monetization does not appear to be overly aggressive. Developer Raptor Byte has said it wants to be as consumer-friendly as possible, with the plan being to release paid DLC for the game. One is already available that adds cosmetics, new gun sights, and the iconic Spas 12 shotgun, so some content will be locked behind a paywall.

Steam's Free-to-Keep Promotion Only Has 1 Free Upcoming Game Confirmed for August 2026

Steam's Free-to-Keep Promotion is usually a great avenue for 100% free PC games, but it seems August might be a slower month.

By Joshua Duckworth

Codename Cure 2 Launches to Mostly Positive Reviews on Steam

Check Out Codename Cure 2 on Steam

Released on July 24 and having amassed over 600 user reviews in that time, Codename Cure 2 is a free-to-play co-op zombie first-person shooter game (trying saying that as a zombie). Up to 5 players squad up and are simply tasked with surviving an endless horde of undead, complete with procedurally generated maps so every run is a little different. Between these deployments, players return to Cure HQ to customize their soldier, unlock new weapons, equip cosmetics, and prepare for new ops. It's a clear-cut zombie game formula, but it works if it's fun, and most players say it is fun.

Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.

Round 1

Which one doesn't belong?

0 / 10
10.0 s

Results

0/5

Best: 0/5

—

More Games

With over 600 reviews, Codename Cure 2 currently sits at a 79% Mostly Positive review rating on Steam, which is a solid launch for a free indie game on Steam. Many reviews highlight its co-op elements, its procedural mission design, and the amount of progression packed into the otherwise smaller game experience, but there's room to grow: visuals can be rough, lighting can be inconsistent, and there's a need for more maps, enemies, and general content for the long-term. One review called it better than Killing Floor 3 . Perhaps one of the biggest issues right now is how quickly players have noticed that every mission, however procedural it may be, ends with a short timer, a horde of zombies, and an extraction, giving mission endings a samesy feel.

When one of the critiques for a new video game is that players want more, that's a pretty good and fair critique, but it's uncertain how much of that will be paid premium DLC for monetization vs. core updates to Codename Cure 2 . Per a dev update, fans can expect the following to be "mostly" free with some paid DLC mixed in: more weapons and sidearms for each class, a new game mode, 1-2 new maps, a new region for Bomb Extraction, new weapon skins, a ping/quick chat system, more customization options, and other quality of life tweaks.

Having a solid launch is, of course, one major hurdle for any video game, but that's especially true for the number of game releases on Steam every day. There are so many released on the storefront every single day that games like Codename Cure 2 can fall to the wayside. As such, fans hopefully stick around for the coming updates.
